title: Serve Robotics Grows Revenue 404% but Cuts Full-Year Outlook
summary: Serve Robotics reported second-quarter 2026 results on August 6, posting revenue of $3.2 million, up 404% year over year and 9% sequentially, with recurring revenue surpassing 50% of total revenue for the first time. The company averaged 792 daily active delivery robots and ended the quarter with $240.4 million in cash and marketable securities. It cut its full-year 2026 revenue guidance to $9-10 million, down from prior guidance, citing lower-than-expected delivery volume through its Uber Eats partnership, even as DoorDash-linked revenue grew nearly 50% sequentially. Serve also signed seven multiyear hospital contract extensions and added two new hospital customers through its Diligent Robotics acquisition, and lowered its non-GAAP FY2026 operating expense outlook to $140-150 million from $160-170 million.
whyItMatters: The mixed print, record year-over-year growth alongside a guidance cut, shows how uneven demand still is for sidewalk and indoor delivery robots even as fleet deployment scales. Investors will read the Uber Eats shortfall as a sign that a single delivery-platform partnership can swing a small robotics operator's outlook meaningfully, and Serve's push into diversified verticals like hospitals and laundry delivery as a hedge against that concentration risk.
